title: Cipher and Ledger
premise: Retired detective Lena Eriksen is paid a suspiciously generous retainer by a nervous accountant, Marta, to prove that her employer, shipping magnate Halvard Brandt, will not be murdered on the thirtieth anniversary of his brother's drowning — a death ruled accidental but whispered to be otherwise. Lena's investigation into the old drowning unravels a forged ledger, a swapped inheritance, and a family built on a lie: Halvard stole his brother's fortune and identity papers the night he died. When the would-be killer turns out to be Marta herself — the drowned brother's secret daughter, raised on a deathbed confession — Lena must choose between the letter of the law and the justice thirty years never delivered. In the end, Lena exposes the truth publicly rather than turning Marta in, the confession forces the estate's restitution, and Lena's ragtag bookshop regulars become the family she never admitted she wanted.
about_author: Ada Iversen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers along the Norwegian coast before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about paper trails, old debts, and the families people build instead of inherit.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Lena, tending her failing bookshop and dodging her own loneliness, is visited by Marta, who pays triple to hire her for a crime that hasn't happened yet. Lena, prideful and broke, takes the case despite its absurdity. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity masking a fear that retirement has made her irrelevant.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Tide
chapters.summary: Lena digs into the drowning of Anders Brandt, 1994, and finds the case file suspiciously thin — the investigating officer retired early and rich. Her bookshop assistant, teenage runaway Theo, proves an unexpectedly gifted researcher. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the old thrill of detection rekindling, tinged with guilt at enjoying it.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Ghost
chapters.summary: Theo finds a mislabeled shipping ledger showing Anders, not Halvard, funded the family fleet. Lena interviews the retired officer, who is terrified and evasive, hinting he was paid to close the file. POV: Lena, with an interlude from the officer's memory. Emotional beat: dread hardening into certainty that this is murder, old and new.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven in Wool
chapters.summary: Lena interviews the Brandt family at their estate: the widow, brittle and watchful; the son, drunk and bitter; Halvard himself, charming and lying. Each alibi for the anniversary night is rehearsed. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the claustrophobic realization that everyone in the house is guarding something.

chapters.title: Client Missing
chapters.summary: Marta vanishes days before the anniversary, leaving her retainer unspent and a locked deposit box key hidden in a book Lena sold her. Theo worries; Lena refuses to report her missing, sensing a trap. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the first crack in Lena's professional armor — she cares about the client.

chapters.title: The Deposit Box
chapters.summary: The box holds Anders's true will, a photograph of Marta as a child with Anders, and a deathbed letter naming Halvard as her father's killer. Lena now knows who Marta is and what she intends. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the case inverts — Lena isn't preventing a murder; she's deciding whether to allow one.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Lena races the clock: the family gathers for the memorial, the widow quietly poisons Halvard's nightly glass as an unrelated insurance policy, and Theo follows Marta to the boathouse. POV: rotating — Lena, Theo, Marta. Emotional beat: converging dread; every thread tightening at once.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Climax. Marta confronts Halvard at the same dock where Anders died; Lena arrives mid-standoff and talks her down not with law but with truth — Halvard's empire is already collapsing, and killing him would erase Anders's legacy rather than restore it. Halvard confesses to the drowning on Marta's hidden recorder. POV: Lena and Marta. Emotional beat: terror, then the fragile mercy of a choice made in the dark.

chapters.title: Confession and Cost
chapters.summary: The recording reaches the widow and son before the police; Halvard, exposed, takes his own exit before arrest. Lena withholds Marta's identity from the investigation, burning her own principles to do it. The widow, knowing, says nothing — her own crime a mutual silence. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: victory that tastes like compromise; justice delivered, law defied.

chapters.title: What the Bookshop Keeps
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the estate pays restitution, Marta takes a quiet job in Lena's shop, Theo officially moves into the back room, and the regulars linger longer than customers should. Lena closes the case file and opens the shop late on purpose. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: found family settling into place — the case she couldn't close is the one that opened her door.
